title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Originals Still Circulating When a Corrected Set Is Issued
content:
A corrected `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` set can only enter circulation in place of the originals it supersedes. This page defines how the originals of the earlier set that are still out in circulation bear on the number of new originals.

## Rule

1. **Figure read.** The figure used is the count of originals still in circulation that the document record shows, as it stands when the corrected set goes out.
2. **Previous set fully back.** The previous set counts as fully back only when that figure is zero, every original of it having come back into the line's hands.
3. **Originals of the new set.** New originals enter circulation with the corrected set only against a document whose figure is zero. While the figure is above zero, the number of new originals is zero.
4. **What the zero records.** A corrected set is issued only onto a document from which every original of the earlier set has come back. A zero under clause 3 is a count of new originals and nothing more; it records that none would go into circulation and confers no standing to issue the set on a document whose figure is above zero.

## Input, judgement, output

| Originals of the earlier set still in circulation at the moment of issue | Previous set fully back? | Effect on new originals |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Yes | New originals may enter circulation |
| 1 | No | None |
| 3 | No | None |

(The figures are hypothetical.)

## Points of judgement

**The documentation history shows two originals handed in, but the document still shows one in circulation. Is the previous set fully back?** No. The test is the figure on the document, and one original is still out.
